description:
Athenance is a multidisciplinary team passionate about technology, science, and space exploration. We bring together skills in Data Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and Data Visualization to transform complex data into meaningful insights.

Our goal is to combine creativity, analytical thinking, and technology to develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges and explore new frontiers.
summary:
Aurora is a crew health-monitoring platform for long-duration missions. It gives astronauts a single place to track their own health, since on deep-space flights they are often the first to notice that something is changing.

Every reading (vital signs, sleep, mental health, labs, radiation and cabin environment) is compared against the astronaut’s own personal baseline, not just population averages. Aurora flags deviations, detects combined patterns such as cabin air quality affecting sleep and stress, and explains each alert in plain language with recommended actions. An AI assistant is available, with a guardrail that discards any answer citing numbers not present in the data.

A dedicated radiation module tracks career dose against NASA’s 600 mSv limit, projects it to the end of the mission, and plans surface excursions based on solar activity.

Aurora supports decision-making rather than diagnosis, helping crews catch immune, cardiovascular, bone and mental-health changes early. It currently runs on synthetic data.
details:
What it does
Aurora is a web platform where each crew member’s health is tracked across six areas: vital signs, sleep and mental health, labs, radiation, and cabin environment. Every measurement is classified as Normal, Attention or Critical by two comparisons, and the worse result wins. The first is a screening reference range for adults. The second is the astronaut’s own baseline: the median and a robust deviation (MAD × 1.4826) of their first 10 mission days. Persistent-event detection and combined-pattern rules link indicators to NASA mission risks (radiation, isolation, closed hostile environment, bone loss, cardiovascular). For example, high cabin CO₂ plus worse sleep or stress triggers a cabin-air alert. Each alert comes with a plain-language explanation and recommended actions.

Radiation module
It uses dose rates measured by the Curiosity RAD instrument (1.84 mSv/day in transit, 0.64 on the surface) to project career dose against NASA’s 600 mSv limit. It also plans Mars surface excursions based on duration, shielding and solar activity.

Super Intelligence assistant
An assistant explains alerts and answers questions, but a guardrail discards any answer that cites a number not in the data, names a disease or drug, or suggests an action outside the rules engine’s list.

Benefits and intended impact
Astronauts on long missions will have limited real-time contact with Earth, so Aurora supports self-monitoring and early detection of immune, cardiovascular, bone and mental-health changes. It is decision support, not diagnosis.

Creativity
Personal baselines instead of population averages, one-click scenarios (sleep debt, radiation event, flu-like illness), and an SI constrained by rules instead of free text.
